examples.text: "Kim, Jack, and I will stand you guys," Jimmie Burdette said. / "We'll smear you!" laughed Ron.

glosses: To position or be positioned socially:
To cover the expense of; to pay for.

examples.text: to stand a round of drinks
to stand a treat
to stand bail (security in respect of an arrested person)

glosses: To position or be positioned socially:
To have or maintain a position, order, or rank; to be in a particular relation.

examples.text: Christian charity, or love, stands first in the rank of gifts.

glosses: To position or be positioned socially:
To be consistent; to agree; to accord.

examples.text: Doubt me not, by Heauen, I vvill doe nothing / But vvhat may ſtand vvith honour: […]

glosses: To position or be positioned socially:
To appear in court.
Of a ship or its captain, to steer, sail (in a specified direction, for a specified destination etc.).

examples.text: To repaire his defects, hee stood for the coast of Calabria, but hearing there was six or seven Galleyes at Mesina hee departed thence for Malta[…].

glosses: To remain without ruin or injury.

examples.text: My mind on its own centre stands unmov'd.

glosses: To stop asking for more cards; to keep one's hand as it has been dealt so far.

examples.text: I took my stand upon an eminence […] to look into their several ladings.

glosses: A defensive position or effort.

examples.text: The Commander says we will make our stand here.

examples.text: They took a firm stand against copyright infringement.

examples.text: They have a four-game stand at home against the Yankees.  They spent the summer touring giving 4 one-night stands a week.
